recipes.name: Peanut Noodles
ingredients_raw: 1 bunch green onions, sliced (white parts only)

steps.text: Cook pasta in a large pot of boiling water until done. Drain.

Meanwhile, combine oil and onions in a small skillet. Saute over low heat until tender. Add ginger; cook and stir for 1 to 2 minutes. Mix in peanut butter, soy sauce, water, vinegar, sugar, and red pepper flakes. Remove from heat.
Toss noodles with sauce, and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Peanut Noodles
raw_recipe.description: Ginger comes alive when its warmed, and it gets that opportunity in this tasty sauce. All the ingredients - peanut butter to sesame oil -are warmed together in a pan until their flavors blend and the sauce becomes flavorful.

video.description: In this video, you’ll see how to make noodles with a simple, savory peanut sauce. Peanut butter combines with minced fresh ginger, soy sauce, a little cider vinegar, and red pepper flakes to create a deeply flavorful sauce to toss with hot noodles. Use your favorite pasta. Spaghetti works great. Or try soba noodles, a traditional buckwheat-flour noodle. If you like, jazz things up with fresh vegetables, like snap peas, carrots, and red bell peppers, for a filling, healthy dinner that’s ready in no time.

review.reviewBody:
Great base recipe. As with most people who gave four or five stars, I tinkered with the proportions. That's not a problem with the recipe, just an issue of personal tastes and preferences. Here are the quantities I used: 
8 ounces spaghetti
1 bunch green onions, sliced (white parts only)
(for the onions, I had access to spring bermuda onions which worked very well)
1 tablespoon sesame oil
1 tablespoon minced fresh ginger root
2 cloves garlic, minced
1/3 + 2 TBS cup peanut butter 
1/8 cup soy sauce
1/3 cup hot water
1 tablespoon cider or rice) vinegar
1 teaspoon white sugar
1/4 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes (I used a couple pinches of cayenne pepper powder)

I reduced the amount of soy because 1/4 cup seemed like too much sodium for me. I also tripled the ginger (1 TBS instead of 1 tsp) because I like a good, strong ginger flavor and it really turned out well. I also increased the water from 1/4 to 1/3 cup since I reduced the amount of liquid when I decreased the soy sauce. I also added a couple cloves of minced garlic which I added to the oil/onions with the ginger. 

As I alluded to before, the sign of a truly good recipe is one that can be easily altered to suit individual preferences! Very happy with this recipe.

Phenomenal recipe! I always get tons of compliments when I bring this to potlucks. Because I like to tweak recipes, I added sliced chicken breast, 1 cup of coarse chopped peanuts, chopped green onions (green and white parts both), snow peas, 2 tbsps of sugar instead of 1 tsp, 2 tbsps of minced ginger, and toasted sesame seeds. The flavor really melds well together, and it's even better the next day!

I kinda winged this one - I love thai peanut sauce, but I hate pad thai (AKA rice noodles). This recipe popped up today with good ratings, so I went for it! I used roughly 1/3 pkg of whole wheat spaghetti, nearly a lb of chicken breast, which I boiled and lightly shredded with a fork, and broccoli, which I blanched just until tender, drained, then briefly sauteed in a bit of sesame oil in my pan. I removed the broccoli from the pan, and added it to the bowl of shredded chicken to keep for later.
I put three cloves of garlic and about 2 inches of ginger root into my cuisinart to mince. It came to about 2-3 tablespoons total. I sauteed with the green onion in sesame, as directed.
Instead of adding straight up white sugar (sounded gross) We have many thai sauces in our fridge. I used a few tablespoons of sweet chili sauce (which has sugar, as well as other spices) and instead of pepper flakes, I used garlic chili sauce (another handy, but spicier thai sauce, both can be found very inexpensive at your local Asian grocer, great to use for dipping sauces or marinades). Used about 1/8 cup or a couple of tablespoons of the low-sodium soy sauce. I added to taste, so as not to go overboard with the salt.
I also added a light pouring of rice vinegar, a small tablespoon or so. 
I had coconut water, so I added that until the sauce loosened up. Mixed in the noodles, chicken and broccoli and topped with chopped roasted peanuts!
Consider sauteing the veggies first, no sugar, use lite soy sauce, substitute lite coconut milk for the water, add extra peanut butter. Good stuff!

We love this recipe, but use it as a base. We add the following, and it makes it so much better: 1) Bite size pieces of cooked chicken. 2) sautee'd veggies (Broccoli, Red Pepper, and Carrot). 3) Instead of the sugar, we use MaePloy sauce or honey. 4) A must-add is to cook whole peanuts in the sauce. 5) A tablespoon (or to taste preference) of minced garlic. 6) Sesame oil. l 7) Garnish heavily with all the green part of the onion. We needed to add extra water to the sauce to thin it. I also cooked fried tofu pieces on the side for myself as the vegetarian in the family. It's a satisfying one-dish meal. You may need to 1.5 or double it depending on how many you have as it saves well. Thumbs up!

These noodles are delicious. I like that it's equally good hot, cold or room temperature. I don't care for ginger so I omitted it. I minced 3 cloves of garlic and softened it with the green onions. I have made it with and without the vinegar and have not been able to tell a difference. I use 1/2 cup of chunky peanut butter, and about 1.5 Tablespoons of honey in addition to the sugar because I like my sauce a bit sweeter. The sesame oil is imperative; you miss a huge layer of flavor if it's not included. I use lo mein noodles, about 12 ounces for the amount of sauce in the basic recipe. Thanks for this excellent recipe.

We've been making this for over 13 years (printed the recipe on 01/31/2010), and it's been a family favorite, in our dinner rotation ever since! My sister recommended it originally, and over the years we have refined it to our preferences (though the original base recipe was a winner to begin with). Here are the things we've adjusted gradually: we as cooked diced chicken, adjust the liquid to 1/2 c chicken broth, and use rice vinegar instead of cider vinegar. We also garnish with chopped peanuts.

Used light soy sauce instead but still found it too salty. Added 2 tablespoons of brown sugar at the end and this mellowed it perfectly. Added my veges at the same time as the ginger and sauted them lightly instead of adding them raw at the end. Would be happy enough to make this dish again with those minor changes.

My Southern fried husband had four helpings! I sauteed chicken and a veggie mix and added them to the finished sauce and served with chopped peanuts on top. I used SDTERP’s quantity modifications for ginger, garlic and sesame oil. This was great. We will definitely make this again. Thank you for sharing!

My, this was delicious and very easy to put together with staples I already had in my pantry. Changes made: I used 1/2 tsp. ground ginger (I had no fresh and was too lazy to make a trip out to get some); tossed the hot drained pasta with a little toasted sesame oil which really added a depth of flavor; added 2 cloves minced garlic (I felt the dish needed it) and 1 carrot, cut into small matchsticks and sautéed them with the onions; finally, garnished the finished dish with chopped roasted peanuts, additional sliced green onions (green part) and toasted sesame seeds. Next time I make this I may add chicken strips or some shrimp. Truly a winning dish.

This is a good starter recipe for Pad Thai type noodles. I diced 4 chicken thighs and sauteed them in some canola oil, then added the onion, garlic and ginger. I used a large clove of garlic and about a tablespoon of chopped ginger. The rest of the ingredients were pretty much as written except I omitted the sugar and used low sodium soy sauce. I used 8 oz whole whole wheat thin spaghetti and tossed the sauce over it, adding more water as needed. We like more heat, so I added more red pepper flakes. To add a bit more flavor, I added 1/4 C chopped peanuts and about 1/4 cup chopped cilantro and topped with some of the sliced green onion tops. I think my peanut butter was a bit old, so next time I'll be sure to use fresh to improve the peanut taste. Some siracha would also be a plus.
I would 2x sauce...
Too much soya sauce. Not enough creamy.
Be careful with the soy sauce, it can really make it too salty.

I only tweaked a little. I used extra crunchy PB. Didn't have sesame oil so Olive oil & sesame seeds it is. No sugar. I did have to add a little more water since it was getting to thick. Taste your sauce when it's almost done to see if you need to add anything else. Remember sauce thickens while cooling down. Noodles were carb overload so I steamed up coleslaw mix & slivered red onion. I added some leftover chicken. Mixed it all up & served.
Not bad but not a repeat for me. The sauce had good flavor, but it was a little dry/thick for me.

This is a great recipe. The first time I followed to a t and it was great. The next few times I measured with my heart, and it still came out great. I’ve used frozen ginger cubes (worked great). Added some shredded carrot and grilled chicken (to add veg and protein) came out great. Substituted cayenne for red pepper flakes (Came out great). So it’s a very forgiving recipe, which comes together super easy!
This sauce is really good. I made exactly as the recipe was listed. I will definitely make this again, but I will use only 1-2 tablespoons. It was too peanut buttery for me.

This was one of the most awful things I have ever made. I don't know if I did something wrong, but it was inedible. The sauce didn't come together and I bought these red lentil noodles on a whim. The combination was gross. Maybe it would taste better if you are more skilled and use traditional ingredients.
I added too much peanut butter but it was really good.
